Web design in Pflugerville, TX has to work for two kinds of customers at once: the neighbor who lives here and the person passing through on a trail, a toll road or a lunch break. Both make their decision on a phone, usually in a few seconds. Dominion Web Design Pro builds a demo of your site first, written for your business and your side of Pflugerville, so you can judge it before you pay anything.

The Trail Capital of Texas, and what that does for local search

In 2025 the Texas Legislature designated Pflugerville the official Trail Capital of Texas for a ten-year period running through 2035. The resolution cites a city staff analysis finding more public trail per person than in any other Texas city, about 1.49 miles for every 2,000 residents. Lake Pflugerville and the Gilleland Creek Trail, the city's longest at about 6.5 miles, pull walkers, runners and cyclists from across the area.

People on a trail are out of their cars, close by and deciding on the spot. They search for coffee, a smoothie, a bike repair, a place to eat with kids. That is the most winnable search there is, because the customer may be a few hundred yards away. Winning it takes almost nothing fancy: correct hours, a working phone number, a map pin in the right place and a site that loads on a weak signal.

Most businesses lose that customer to a competitor with a worse product and better information. The fix is cheap, and it is the first thing we set up.

Pflugerville's main business corridors

The 2020 census counted about 65,000 people in Pflugerville. Its businesses sit in a few distinct places, and each one sees a different kind of customer.

Old Town and Pecan Street

The historic center, with restaurants, salons, small offices and the shops locals walk to. Customers here want hours, parking and a menu or price list.

SH 130 and SH 45

The toll roads brought business parks, Stone Hill Town Center and the bigger retail. Drivers here search by what they need and how far off the exit it is.

FM 685 and the neighborhoods

Home services, clinics, daycares and fitness studios serving the subdivisions. These customers compare two or three options before they call.

A business that started here and stayed

Community Impact, the hyperlocal news company, was founded in 2005 by John and Jennifer Garrett. Its first edition covered Round Rock and Pflugerville, and it started with a small team working out of the Garretts' house. When it needed a real headquarters, it built one in the 130 Commerce Center in east Pflugerville, under a 2012 agreement with the city and the Pflugerville Community Development Corporation. It still runs from there, with offices in Houston, Dallas and San Antonio.

The usual story is that a small-town business outgrows its town and moves to the city. This one did not, and it says something about Pflugerville as a place to run a business that intends to grow.

If you have the same plan, build your website for it from the start. Choose a domain and a structure that can hold pages for Round Rock, Hutto, Manor and Northeast Austin later, even if you only serve Pflugerville today. Adding pages to a well-built site is easy. Rebuilding a site that was never meant to grow is not.

Web design in Pflugerville, TX for people who work in town

Pflugerville has long tried to be a place where people can live and work in the same city instead of commuting into Austin every day. Every resident who works locally is a resident who is in town at lunchtime, needs an oil change on a Tuesday and books a haircut for after work.

That customer is in a hurry. Your site needs to answer three questions immediately: are you open, how far away are you, and how do I book or call. A service page that buries the phone number under three paragraphs about your passion loses them.

For trades and shops like that, the small business website package does the job: five hand-written pages, a form that emails you every lead, your map and hours, and the search basics submitted to Google.

A page plan for a Pflugerville home service company

Many Pflugerville businesses are trades and home services working the subdivisions and the towns around them: lawn care, pest control, pool service, roofing, garage doors. For a company like that, here is roughly how we would lay out a Pro build.

PageWhat it does
HomeSays what you do, that you are based in Pflugerville, and how to call, all above the fold on a phone.
One page per main serviceAnswers the questions customers ask about that service, with photos of real jobs and how pricing works.
AboutWho owns the company, how long you have lived in the area if you want to share it, and who will show up at the door.
GalleryBefore and after photos from local jobs, with the neighborhood named when the customer agrees.
City pagesRound Rock, Hutto, Manor, Wells Branch and other towns you serve, each researched and written for that place.
ContactA short form that emails you every lead, your phone, hours and service area.

The order matters too. The home page and the main service pages go first, because they carry most of the calls. City pages follow, each one written only after looking at what that town actually needs, so the Hutto page talks about Hutto rather than repeating the Pflugerville page with the name swapped.

That is the Pro package at $997 one time. If you only work in Pflugerville, Starter at $497 covers the essentials, and you can add city pages later.

Where Pflugerville owners can get free help

The Pflugerville Chamber of Commerce runs member networking, ribbon cuttings and tourism work, and in 2025 the city was given the Tourism Friendly Texas designation by the state. SCORE's Austin chapter offers free one-on-one mentoring for owners in the area, and the Texas State University Small Business Development Center, based in Austin and serving Travis and Williamson counties, provides no-cost or low-cost confidential counseling. We are not connected to any of them. They are simply useful.

Common questions

Who builds small business websites in Pflugerville, TX?

Plenty of Austin-area agencies will take the job. Dominion Web Design Pro is a small East Texas business run by Maurice Johnson, who writes and builds each site himself and shows you a free demo first. We have no office in Pflugerville; the work is done remotely and delivered by link, phone and email.

What does a website cost for a Pflugerville small business?

Our prices are one time: Starter $497 (5 pages), Pro $997 (10 pages plus 10 city pages) and Agency $1,997 (keyword research and a page for every town-and-service combination worth having). Hosting and maintenance are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent. The website designer cost guide shows how that compares with typical rates.

What should I fix first: my website or my Google listing?

Your Google Business Profile, if it is empty or wrong. It is free and it controls the map results people see first. Then make sure your website says the same thing: the same name, phone, hours and address. The two should back each other up.

Can my website cover Round Rock, Hutto and Manor too?

Yes, if you really serve them. A service-area page can name them on any package, and the Pro package adds ten city pages, each researched and written for that town rather than copied from the Pflugerville page with the name changed.
